native_scope: All three original bounded tasks matched their reference answers without model calls. Core extraction was timed 30 times per candidate with input in memory; no interpreter startup, serialization, file IO, network or outer-agent cost is included.
parser_scope: Go compiler location lines, wanted parameter signatures, missing-interface-method names, and process exit codes. findings.stronger_baseline: gh plus a short rg filter achieved most of the CI savings seen previously. The older window prototype is only 1.88% below this stronger baseline in total usage.
findings.internal_agent: Computing the compiler facts internally reduced total agent usage by 4.47% and uncached input by 8.24% versus gh+rg in this case. All outer-agent methods still used one shell call.
findings.native_only: For these deterministic evidence-extraction tasks the internal code can finish with zero model calls and zero model tokens. An agent invocation and model-written reply still consume tokens and are not included in the zero figure.
findings.interpretation: The useful optimization is to complete bounded, deterministic parsing internally and return small structured facts. Generic error interpretation, fixes and arbitrary review understanding remain outside the tested native scope.
findings.packaging: The same deterministic code could be invoked by a CLI or by a skill script; this experiment does not establish that the packaging itself saves tokens.

limitations: One public CI case with three sessions per arm; not a broad savings or reliability estimate.

The stronger baseline/internal arms were measured after the earlier arms, rather than fully interleaved with them. Same task/model/snapshot were used, but cross-run cache or server variations are possible.
Both method guides count toward input usage and their text differs naturally.
Compiler facts are syntax extraction, not general root-cause diagnosis or a successful code fix. Unknown formats fall back to complete original evidence.
Native-only zero tokens refer to the deterministic component without a model. Creating the implementation, preparing the benchmark and an outer agent call all have separate costs.
Native timings cover only in-memory extraction; they are not complete GitHub workflow latency measurements.
Native review and delta answers cover the original metadata tasks. They do not perform semantic review interpretation, code repair or persistent change tracking.
Reported input-plus-output includes cached input; output already includes reasoning tokens. Monetary cost is not calculated.
These remain offline validation prototypes, not new tools github product commands.
All six additional trials are included; no retries or discarded trials.
